links.outcome: Model recognition of answer absence under none-of-the-above perturbation of exam items
links.effect: Strong exam accuracy (frontier models 81.9%-86.4%) did not guarantee reliable recognition of answer absence under none-of-the-above perturbation testing.
links.quote: However, expert-rated rationale assessment and none-of-the-above perturbation testing revealed that strong examination accuracy did not guarantee high-quality explanatory support or reliable recognition of answer absence, indicating that examination performance and answer-selection robustness represent related but distinct dimensions of model behavior.

links.outcome: Whether exam accuracy reflects quality of explanatory support and robustness
links.effect: Frontier LLMs scored 81.9%-86.4% on the exam, but expert-rated rationales and answer-absence recognition showed exam accuracy did not guarantee high-quality reasoning or robustness.
links.quote: However, expert-rated rationale assessment and none-of-the-above perturbation testing revealed that strong examination accuracy did not guarantee high-quality explanatory support or reliable recognition of answer absence, indicating that examination performance and answer-selection robustness represent related but distinct dimensions of model behavior.

unlisted_practices: Item-level psychometric (classical and IRT) analysis of LLM exam performance against human resident difficulty and distractor data

screen.reason: Evaluates multiple LLMs on a cardiology residency examination benchmark using psychometric and perturbation analysis without testing an organizational deployment guardrail or practice.
